meta.title: Alexandre Mandra · Software Engineer
meta.description: Paris-based Software Engineer: web data acquisition, ingestion pipelines and applied generative AI.

hero.title: I'm a developer who builds tools
hero.lead: Data collection, applied AI, real-time applications. What I enjoy: building a project from start to finish, solving the technical problems along the way, and seeing people use what I've built.

heroDemo.prompt: Which games did Naughty Dog make?
heroDemo.note: Crash Bandicoot 4 is a Toys for Bob game. Naughty Dog created Crash in the 90s: it's the plausible mistake, the hardest one to spot.

projects.title: What I've built
projects.lead: At work, I build data systems. In my spare time, I mostly build games: that's where I experiment with real-time, physics and multiplayer.

hunter.title: hallucination-hunter
hunter.desc: A local LLM (Qwen 3 via Ollama) lists the video games of 22 studios, and every answer is checked against Wikidata. Result: only a minority of the cited games are right, and the model credits real games to the wrong studio more often than it invents them. With a Streamlit dashboard to follow the runs and test any studio.

blindtest.title: Blind Test
blindtest.desc: The engine behind a multiplayer music quiz: rooms, buzzers, scores and timer synced in real time between the host and players, who join from their phones via QR code. The server owns the timer: it pauses on the first buzz and resumes on a wrong answer.

wheel.title: Wheel of Fortune
wheel.desc: Every morning, my team spins it to pick who runs the daily meeting. Animated draw, TV mode, automatic saving.

dispatch.title: Dispatch Dub
dispatch.desc: The idea: a French dub for Dispatch, a narrative game only available in English. I figured out how the game stores its dialogue, then built an Electron app that swaps the audio files based on the language the player picks. The project stopped because I couldn't put together a team of voice actors.

towerdash.title: TowerDash
towerdash.desc: A low-poly battle royale built as a team at ESGI: the goal was to reach the top of a tower while eliminating opponents. It ran on mobile, with a website recapping match scores.

worms.title: Worms in Python
worms.desc: A turn-based artillery game inspired by Worms, built as a duo with Pygame: gravity-based trajectories, randomly generated terrain, several weapons, explosions and health points. A few sleepless nights on the clock.

idea.title: From idea to project
idea.text: I start by listing the features the project needs. If it relies on APIs or external services, I compare what's available and what it costs before choosing.

ai.title: AI as a tool, not a replacement
ai.text: I describe the project to Claude as precisely as I can, it proposes a plan, I correct it, then we move forward step by step, testing every part along the way. To me, AI doesn't replace developers: it's a tool that makes me more creative and more productive.

data.title: Data you can trust
data.text: Data is only worth something if you can trust it. Normalization, deduplication and quality monitoring are part of my pipelines.

secure.title: Secure, and actually used
secure.text: Two things matter most to me: that a project is secure, and that the people using it like it. A tool nobody uses hasn't done its job.

code.title: Code others can pick up
code.text: I like leaving my mark on a project, but in a way that whoever comes after me can understand it and take it over easily.

about.title: A detour through games, a return to the web
paragraphs: I discovered development during my two-year degree in Digital Systems in Amiens. That's where the door opened.

I then started a Bachelor in 3D & Video Games at ESGI: working in games was a goal of mine. But as the year went on, it stopped being what I enjoyed. I went back to my first love, the web, and continued all the way to a master's level degree in software engineering.
Today I work on data and applied AI, and what drives me hasn't changed: building something from start to finish, solving the problems that come up, and seeing people use it.
I also always have project ideas in mind. Many stay ideas; the ones that make it are on this page.

sections.title: Contact form and personal data
body: The information you enter in the form (name, email, topic, message) is only used to reply to you. It is sent by email through the Resend service and is not stored on this site.
The form is protected against spam by Cloudflare Turnstile, which analyzes technical signals from your browser to tell humans from bots.
Vercel, Resend and Cloudflare are service providers based in the United States; their processing is governed by their own contractual commitments and privacy policies.

Under the GDPR, you have the right to access, correct and delete your data. To exercise it, use the contact form. You can also file a complaint with the CNIL, the French data protection authority (cnil.fr).

sections.title: Cookies and local storage
body: This site uses no advertising cookies and no analytics. It only stores two preferences in your browser: your chosen language (NEXT_LOCALE cookie) and the light or dark theme (local storage). These are needed for the site to work and do not require consent.
